q: Every reaction has a rate, or _____, at which it proceeds.
e: Every reaction has a rate, or speed, at which it proceeds. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The study of reaction rate is known as _____.
e: The study of reaction rate is known as chemical kinetics. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: An explosion of dynamite and striking of a match take within a _____.
e: An explosion of dynamite and striking of a match take within a second. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Weathering of rocks and rusting of an iron pipe happen for _____.
e: Weathering of rocks and rusting of an iron pipe happen for years. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Depletion of the ozone layer depends on the relative rates of reactions that produce and destroy _____ molecules.
e: Depletion of the ozone layer depends on the relative rates of reactions that produce and destroy ozone molecules. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Enzyme action is essential in food _____.
e: Enzyme action is essential in food preservatives. Enzymes are protein catalysts that speed specific biochemical reactions.

q: The economical synthesis of ammonia to produce fertiliser depends on the rate at which gaseous nitrogen and hydrogen can be converted to _____.
e: The economical synthesis of ammonia to produce fertiliser depends on the rate at which gaseous nitrogen and hydrogen can be converted to ammonia. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Knowledge of reaction rates is required in drug design, pollution control, and food _____.
e: Knowledge of reaction rates is required in drug design, pollution control, and food processing. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the _____ is.
e: Rate is a measure of how fast or how slow the reaction is. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the _____ taken for that change.
e: The rate of reaction means measuring the change in the amount of a product produced or a reactant used up in the time taken for that change. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: White phosphorus bursts into flames when exposed to _____.
e: White phosphorus bursts into flames when exposed to air. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Candle wax burns only after the wick of the candle is _____.
e: Candle wax burns only after the wick of the candle is lighted. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in _____.
e: If the substance is a gas, the amount consumed or formed is expressed in pressure units or as measured in volume. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: _____ units are used if the reactant or product is in solution.
e: Concentration units are used if the reactant or product is in solution. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Generally, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured at a constant _____.
e: Generally, the rate of a reaction in solution is measured at a constant temperature. Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so more collisions have enough energy to react.

q: In the rate expression, the delta ($\Delta$) means _____.
e: In the rate expression, the delta (delta) means change. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the rate expression, the square bracket [] represents _____ concentration.
e: In the rate expression, the square bracket [] represents molar concentration. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The minus (-) sign in the rate of reactant used up means a _____ in the concentration.
e: The minus (-) sign in the rate of reactant used up means a decrease in the concentration. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The plus (+) sign means an _____ in the concentration of the product.
e: The plus (+) sign means an increase in the concentration of the product. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Rate is expressed as a _____ quantity.
e: Rate is expressed as a positive quantity. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In a general chemical reaction, $k$ is the rate constant, which explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the _____ of a chemical reaction.
e: In a general chemical reaction, k is the rate constant, which explains the relationship between the molar concentration of the reactants and the rate of a chemical reaction. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in _____ of products and reactants.
e: The mole ratios from the balanced chemical equation can be used to determine the rates of change in concentrations of products and reactants. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: Different chemical reactions occur at different _____.
e: Different chemical reactions occur at different rates. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or _____).
e: The time measurement is expressed in whatever units fit the reaction (seconds, minutes, hours, days, months or centuries). The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The rate of reaction varies greatly for different reactions and under different _____.
e: The rate of reaction varies greatly for different reactions and under different conditions. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Collision theory explains how chemical reactions occur and is based on the kinetic molecular theory of _____.
e: Collision theory explains how chemical reactions occur and is based on the kinetic molecular theory of gases. Collision theory says particles must hit with the right orientation and enough energy or no reaction happens.

q: Reactant particles moving in random directions possess _____ energy.
e: Reactant particles moving in random directions possess kinetic energy. Chemical energy is stored in bonds.

q: When reactant particles frequently collide with one another, the energy is _____ as a result of the collision.
e: When reactant particles frequently collide with one another, the energy is transferred as a result of the collision. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Not all collisions between reactant particles result in the formation of reaction _____.
e: Not all collisions between reactant particles result in the formation of reaction products. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: During a collision, the spatial _____ of the reactant molecules is important to determine whether or not a reaction occurs.
e: During a collision, the spatial orientation of the reactant molecules is important to determine whether or not a reaction occurs. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: If the colliding particles have the incorrect orientation, they will _____ off each other.
e: If the colliding particles have the incorrect orientation, they will bounce off each other. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The unsuccessful collisions with insufficient energy do not produce a _____.
e: The unsuccessful collisions with insufficient energy do not produce a reaction. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful collisions between reactant _____.
e: The rate of reaction depends on the rate of successful collisions between reactant particles. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the activated complex, which is a _____ species.
e: Reacting particles must collide with sufficient energy to form the activated complex, which is a temporary species. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: In the molecular view, chemical reactions depend on the collisions between atoms, molecules or _____.
e: In the molecular view, chemical reactions depend on the collisions between atoms, molecules or ions. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the frequency of collision _____.
e: According to the collision theory, a reaction will speed up if the frequency of collision increases. Collision theory says particles must hit with the right orientation and enough energy or no reaction happens.

q: A reaction will speed up if the proportion of particles with energy greater than the activation energy _____.
e: A reaction will speed up if the proportion of particles with energy greater than the activation energy increases. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: Collision theory can be used to explain the main factors affecting the rate of chemical _____.
e: Collision theory can be used to explain the main factors affecting the rate of chemical reactions. Collision theory says particles must hit with the right orientation and enough energy or no reaction happens.

q: The activation energy ($E_a$) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a successful _____ to take place.
e: The activation energy (Ea) is the minimum energy that reactant particles must possess for a successful melting to take place. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: During the progress of a reaction, an unstable intermediate known as an activated complex is formed before producing a _____.
e: During the progress of a reaction, an unstable intermediate known as an activated complex is formed before producing a product. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an unstable intermediate _____ which exists for a short time.
e: A hydrogen molecule and an iodine molecule collide to form an unstable intermediate [H2I2] which exists for a short time. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In order to get the product, the reactants must pass through a short-lived, high-energy _____ state.
e: In order to get the product, the reactants must pass through a short-lived, high-energy transition state. Transition metals have a partly filled d subshell in the atom or in a common ion.

q: The minimum energy that needs to be reached in the transition state is equal to the _____ for that reaction.
e: The minimum energy that needs to be reached in the transition state is equal to the activation energy for that reaction. Kinetic energy is energy of motion.

q: The activation energy represents an energy _____ for the reaction.
e: The activation energy represents an energy barrier for the reaction. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: In the reaction between $H_2$ gas and $I_2$ gas to form $HI$, the reaction is the _____ reaction.
e: In the reaction between H2 gas and I2 gas to form HI, the reaction is the exothermic reaction. Endothermic means heat is taken in and delta H is positive. Isothermal: thermal energy is heat.

q: Some energy is _____ when the activated complex leads to the formation of the products in an exothermic reaction.
e: Some energy is released when the activated complex leads to the formation of the products in an exothermic reaction. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: If the energy is not enough to overcome the energy barrier, the decomposition of the product back to _____ will occur.
e: If the energy is not enough to overcome the energy barrier, the decomposition of the product back to reactants will occur. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: A high $E_a$ means that relatively few collisions have the required energy, and hence, the reaction rate is _____.
e: A high Ea means that relatively few collisions have the required energy, and hence, the reaction rate is slow. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: With a low $E_a$, more collisions have sufficient energy to react, and the reaction rate is _____.
e: With a low Ea, more collisions have sufficient energy to react, and the reaction rate is fast. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: A successful collision is a collision that causes a chemical _____.
e: A successful collision is a collision that causes a chemical reaction. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Transition state is also known as an _____ state.
e: Transition state is also known as an intermediate state. The transition state is that unstable high-energy point on the reaction path between reactants and products.

q: Reacting particles must collide in the correct orientation with sufficient energy to overcome the energy _____ to react.
e: Reacting particles must collide in the correct orientation with sufficient energy to overcome the energy barrier to react. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The more successful collisions there are, the more the activated complex leads to the rate of a reaction being _____.
e: The more successful collisions there are, the more the activated complex leads to the rate of a reaction being faster. The activated complex is a short-lived, high-energy arrangement that can split to products or fall back to reactants.

q: The controlled burning of fuel in an internal combustion engine is required to avoid fire or _____.
e: The controlled burning of fuel in an internal combustion engine is required to avoid fire or freezing. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: For many reactions involving liquids or gases, increasing the concentrations of the reactants _____ the rate of reactions.
e: For many reactions involving liquids or gases, increasing the concentrations of the reactants increases the rate of reactions. Higher concentration means more particles in the same volume, so more collisions.

q: If more molecules of the reactants are in the reaction area, there is a greater chance of more effective collisions per unit _____.
e: If more molecules of the reactants are in the reaction area, there is a greater chance of more effective collisions per unit time. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Zinc granule reacts fairly slowly with $1.0 \text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ dilute hydrochloric acid but much faster with _____ $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$ hydrochloric acid.
e: Zinc granule reacts fairly slowly with 1.0 mol dm-3 dilute hydrochloric acid but much faster with 0.1 moldm-3 hydrochloric acid.

q: In reactions involving solids, a reaction occurs at the boundary _____ between reactants.
e: In reactions involving solids, a reaction occurs at the boundary surface between reactants. Core electrons stay inner and do not bond.

q: The rate of a reaction involving a solid reactant is increased by increasing the surface area of the _____.
e: The rate of a reaction involving a solid reactant is increased by increasing the surface area of the solid. A larger surface area gives more places to collide, so a powdered solid usually reacts faster than a lump.

q: The _____ the particle size, the larger the surface area will be.
e: The smaller the particle size, the larger the surface area will be. A larger surface area gives more places to collide, so a powdered solid usually reacts faster than a lump.

q: Aluminium foil reacts moderately with sodium hydroxide solution only when warmed, but powdered aluminium reacts rapidly in the _____.
e: Aluminium foil reacts moderately with sodium hydroxide solution only when warmed, but powdered aluminium reacts rapidly in the cold. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Large pieces of wood are difficult to ignite whereas small pieces burn more _____.
e: Large pieces of wood are difficult to ignite whereas small pieces burn more rapidly. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Reducing the size of particles increases the surface area and the number of effective collisions, thus increasing the rate of _____.
e: Reducing the size of particles increases the surface area and the number of effective collisions, thus increasing the rate of cooling. A larger surface area gives more places to collide, so a powdered solid usually reacts faster than a lump.

q: Changing the pressure does not affect the rate of reaction that only involves solids or _____.
e: Changing the pressure does not affect the rate of reaction that only involves solids or liquids. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The pressure is inversely proportional to the volume of a gas at a constant _____.
e: The pressure is inversely proportional to the volume of a gas at a constant temperature. Raising the pressure of a gas crushes more particles into the same volume and can speed collisions.

q: At low pressure, the volume becomes larger, the number of collisions is smaller, and the rate of reaction is _____.
e: At low pressure, the volume becomes larger, the number of collisions is smaller, and the rate of reaction is explosive. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: At high pressure, the volume becomes smaller, the number of collisions is greater, and the rate of reaction is _____.
e: At high pressure, the volume becomes smaller, the number of collisions is greater, and the rate of reaction is faster. Particles must collide with enough energy and the right orientation to react.

q: Food can cook faster in a pressure cooker because trapped steam becomes hotter as the pressure _____.
e: Food can cook faster in a pressure cooker because trapped steam becomes hotter as the pressure remains constant. The because-clause is the chemical reason that makes the statement hold.

q: Most chemical reactions react faster at a high temperature than at a low _____.
e: Most chemical reactions react faster at a high temperature than at a low temperature. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: The kinetic energy of a gas is directly proportional to the _____.
e: The kinetic energy of a gas is directly proportional to the temperature. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Increasing the temperature increases the kinetic energy, meaning molecules collide more frequently with sufficient _____ energy.
e: Increasing the temperature increases the kinetic energy, meaning molecules collide more frequently with sufficient activation energy. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: The time required to hard-boil an egg in water is much shorter at $100^\circ\text{C}$ than at _____ $^\circ\text{C}$.
e: The time required to hard-boil an egg in water is much shorter at 100degreesC than at 90 degreesC. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Foods are cooled or frozen to slow down the chemical reactions that result in the spoiling of food and the souring of _____.
e: Foods are cooled or frozen to slow down the chemical reactions that result in the spoiling of food and the souring of milk. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the Boltzmann distribution curve, the area under the curve represents the number of particles within a certain _____ range.
e: In the Boltzmann distribution curve, the area under the curve represents the number of particles within a certain energy range. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: In the Boltzmann distribution, the shaded area shows the number of particles with energy greater than the _____ energy.
e: In the Boltzmann distribution, the shaded area shows the number of particles with energy greater than the activation energy. Kinetic energy is energy of motion.

q: When the temperature is increased, the distribution curve flattens and spreads out, showing the fraction of molecules with energy greater than $E_a$ is much _____.
e: When the temperature is increased, the distribution curve flattens and spreads out, showing the fraction of molecules with energy greater than Ea is much larger. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: Generally, for a _____ degrees rise in temperature, the area under the curve approximately doubles.
e: Generally, for a ten degrees rise in temperature, the area under the curve approximately doubles. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: A catalyst is defined as a substance which alters the rate of a chemical reaction but remains chemically _____ at the end.
e: A catalyst is defined as a substance which alters the rate of a chemical reaction but remains chemically destroyed at the end. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Most catalysts make chemical reactions go faster and these are known as _____ catalysts.
e: Most catalysts make chemical reactions go faster and these are known as positive catalysts. A catalyst changes rate by opening a new path and is not used up overall.

q: The most common positive catalyst used in the Haber Process for manufacturing ammonia is _____.
e: The most common positive catalyst used in the Haber Process for manufacturing ammonia is iron. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: In the Contact Process for manufacturing sulphur trioxide, the catalyst used is vanadium(V) oxide or _____ asbestos.
e: In the Contact Process for manufacturing sulphur trioxide, the catalyst used is vanadium(V) oxide or manganese asbestos. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, the catalyst used is manganese(IV) _____.
e: In the preparation of oxygen from hydrogen peroxide, the catalyst used is manganese(IV) oxide. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Sometimes a chemical reaction needs to go more slowly; this kind of catalyst is known as a _____ catalyst.
e: Sometimes a chemical reaction needs to go more slowly; this kind of catalyst is known as a negative catalyst. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Alcohol acts as a negative catalyst to slow down the oxidation of sodium sulphite to sodium _____.
e: Alcohol acts as a negative catalyst to slow down the oxidation of sodium sulphite to sodium sulphur. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Generally, the catalysts provide an alternative pathway for the reaction with lower _____ energy.
e: Generally, the catalysts provide an alternative pathway for the reaction with lower activation energy. Kinetic energy is energy of motion.

q: In the energy diagram, the activation energy of a catalysed reaction is _____ than that of an uncatalysed reaction.
e: In the energy diagram, the activation energy of a catalysed reaction is less than that of an uncatalysed reaction. Activation energy is the minimum energy colliding particles need before they can form products.

q: Catalysts may be homogeneous, or _____, in which case the catalyst and the reactants are in different phases.
e: Catalysts may be homogeneous, or liquid, in which case the catalyst and the reactants are in different phases. Heterogeneous means more than one phase.

q: Homogeneous catalysts most often catalyse the gaseous and aqueous reactions to increase their reaction _____.
e: Homogeneous catalysts most often catalyse the gaseous and aqueous reactions to increase their reaction rates. A homogeneous catalyst is in the same phase as the reactants.

q: In the Lead chamber process, nitrogen oxide acts as a catalyst with no net loss of gas _____ in the overall reaction.
e: In the Lead chamber process, nitrogen oxide acts as a catalyst with no net loss of gas NO in the overall reaction. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Most heterogeneous catalysts are solids that catalyse either gaseous or liquid _____.
e: Most heterogeneous catalysts are solids that catalyse either gaseous or liquid solvents. A heterogeneous catalyst sits in a different phase from the reactants, often a solid with gas or liquid.

q: The reactions take place on the surface of the solid catalyst to speed _____.
e: The reactions take place on the surface of the solid catalyst to speed up. A catalyst speeds or slows a reaction by changing the path, but it is not used up in the overall equation.

q: Enzymes act as biocatalysts for specific biochemical reactions in living _____.
e: Enzymes act as biocatalysts for specific biochemical reactions in living rocks. A catalyst changes rate by opening a new path and is not used up overall.

q: The most well-known digestive enzymes are ptyalin in saliva and _____ in gastric juice.
e: The most well-known digestive enzymes are ptyalin in saliva and lipase in gastric juice. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Digestive enzymes catalyse to hasten the breakdown of large molecules into simpler _____.
e: Digestive enzymes catalyse to hasten the breakdown of large molecules into simpler molecules. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The reaction rate using enzymes is often increased by a factor of $10^6$ to _____.
e: The reaction rate using enzymes is often increased by a factor of 106 to 1012. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Reactions that are initiated by light are called _____ reactions.
e: Reactions that are initiated by light are called photochemical reactions. Thermal energy is heat. Chemical energy is stored in bonds.

q: The brighter the light, the _____ is the reaction.
e: The brighter the light, the faster is the reaction. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: If the intensity of light is greater, a photochemical reaction takes place, such as _____ in green plants.
e: If the intensity of light is greater, a photochemical reaction takes place, such as photosynthesis in green plants. In photosynthesis plants use sunlight, carbon dioxide, and water to make food, and oxygen comes out as a product.

q: The reaction between hydrogen and chlorine becomes explosive when exposed to intense sunlight via a _____ reaction.
e: The reaction between hydrogen and chlorine becomes explosive when exposed to intense sunlight via a nuclear reaction. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: When large amounts of flammable powdered substances collect in grain elevators, violent _____ can occur.
e: When large amounts of flammable powdered substances collect in grain elevators, violent explosions can occur. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Storage of preserved foods at a sub-zero temperature is effective in slowing the rate of bacterial _____.
e: Storage of preserved foods at a sub-zero temperature is effective in slowing the rate of bacterial decay. Higher temperature makes particles move faster, so more collisions have enough energy to react.

q: At high altitudes with low pressure, water boils at a temperature lower than $100^\circ\text{C}$, so it takes a longer time to boil an _____.
e: At high altitudes with low pressure, water boils at a temperature lower than 100degreesC, so it takes a longer time to boil an onion. Higher temperature means a larger fraction of particles have energy at least Ea.

q: In many industrial processes, enzymes are used such as the conversion of glucose to sweeter-tasting _____.
e: In many industrial processes, enzymes are used such as the conversion of glucose to sweeter-tasting fructose. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: Corrosion inhibitors like imidazoline and quaternary amine prevent $H_2S$ and $CO_2$ _____.
e: Corrosion inhibitors like imidazoline and quaternary amine prevent H2S and CO2 corrosion. Amines are organic bases with a nitrogen that can accept a proton.

q: Volatile corrosion inhibitors (VCI) such as morpholine or hydrazine prevent corrosion in _____.
e: Volatile corrosion inhibitors (VCI) such as morpholine or hydrazine prevent corrosion in tanks. pH is the negative log of [H+], so a smaller pH means a more acidic solution.

q: Wrapping metals in volatile corrosion inhibitor-coated paper is common for short-term protection against moisture and _____.
e: Wrapping metals in volatile corrosion inhibitor-coated paper is common for short-term protection against moisture and humidity. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The unit for the rate of a chemical reaction in solution is typically expressed as change in concentration per unit _____.
e: The unit for the rate of a chemical reaction in solution is typically expressed as change in concentration per unit time. Higher concentration means more particles in the same space, so successful collisions happen more often.

q: A catalyst which is in the different phases of the reactants is known as _____ catalyst.
e: A catalyst which is in the different phases of the reactants is known as heterogeneous catalyst. Homogeneous means the same phase.

q: The correct _____ of reactant molecules leads to the formation of products.
e: The correct orientation of reactant molecules leads to the formation of products. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.

q: The reaction time is _____ proportional to the rate.
e: The reaction time is inversely proportional to the rate. The direction of this chemical relationship is the one chemists actually measure.
